DETAILED ACTION
Notice of Pre-AIA  or AIA  Status
The present application, filed on or after March 16, 2013, is being examined under the first inventor to file provisions of the AIA .
Priority
Receipt is acknowledged of certified copies of papers required by 37 CFR 1.55. Copies of Chinese Applications CN201921011114.0; CN201910591817.3; CN201910585250.9; CN201910591847.4; CN201910684842.6; CN201921682904.1; CN201910953740.X; CN201910954105.3; CN201910953826.2; and CN201910954116.1 have been filed with priority dates of 01 July 2019; 01 July 2019; 01 July 2019; 01 July 2019; 26 July 2019; 09 October 2019; 09 October 2019; 09 October 2019; 09 October 2019; and 09 October 2019 respectively.
EXAMINER’S AMENDMENT
An examiner’s amendment to the record appears below. Should the changes and/or additions be unacceptable to applicant, an amendment may be filed as provided by 37 CFR 1.312. To ensure consideration of such an amendment, it MUST be submitted no later than the payment of the issue fee.
Authorization for this examiner’s amendment was given in an interview with Michael Wiersch on 17 January 2025.
The application has been amended as follows:
Claim 1. (Currently Amended) A method for performing a PCR reaction using a PCR reaction system, the PCR reaction system comprising:
a sample containing unit having a pyrolysis freeze-dried powder and a sample provided
a diluent containing unit having a diluent provided therein, the diluent containing unit comprising a diluent outlet;
a PCR reaction unit having a freeze-dried powder of a reverse transcriptase and PCR raw materials provided, the PCR reaction unit comprising a PCR reaction solution outlet and a pyrolyzed sample mixture inlet; and
a piston unit comprising an injection chamber and a piston, the injection chamber comprising a second liquid outlet/inlet,
wherein the second liquid outlet/inlet is connected to the first liquid outlet/inlet through a first pipeline, the second liquid outlet/inlet is connected to the diluent outlet through a second pipeline, the second liquid outlet/inlet is connected to the pyrolyzed sample mixture inlet through a third pipeline, and the PCR reaction solution outlet is connected to the diluent outlet through a fourth pipeline,
the method comprising:
subjecting the piston to a first movement processing, to allow a part of the diluent to enter the injection chamber, wherein the diluent is provided in the diluent containing unit;
subjecting the piston to a second movement processing, to subject the part of the diluent entering the injection chamber, the pyrolysis freeze-dried powder, and the sample to a first mixing processing, wherein the pyrolysis freeze-dried powder and the sample are provided in the sample containing unit, and the first mixing processing is performed in the sample containing unit;
subjecting a product of the first mixing processing to a pyrolysis processing, wherein the pyrolysis processing is performed in the sample containing unit;
subjecting the piston to a third movement processing, to allow a product of the pyrolysis processing to enter the injection chamber;
subjecting the piston to a fourth movement processing, to subject the product of the pyrolysis processing entering the injection chamber and the remaining part of the diluent to a second mixing processing, wherein the second mixing processing is performed in the diluent containing unit;
subjecting the piston to a fifth movement processing, to allow a product of the second mixing processing to enter the injection chamber;
subjecting the piston to a sixth movement processing, to subject the product of the second mixing processing entering the injection chamber and the freeze-dried powder of the reverse transcriptase and the PCR raw materials to a third mixing processing, wherein the freeze-dried powder of the reverse transcriptase and the PCR raw materials is provided in the PCR reaction unit, and the third mixing processing is performed in the PCR reaction unit; and
subjecting a product of the third mixing processing to a PCR temperature cycle amplification processing, wherein the PCR temperature cycle amplification processing is performed in the PCR reaction unit.
Claim 18. (Currently Amended) The system according to claim 16, wherein the sealing film has a thickness ranging from 0.01 mm to 0.2 mm
Claim 19. (Currently Amended) The system according to claim 11, wherein the freeze-dried powder of the pyrolysis raw materials comprises a metal ion chelating agent, sodium dodecyl sulfate, saponin, proteinase K, polyethylene glycol 3350, Tris-HCl, and water; and
the freeze-dried powder of the reverse transcriptase and the PCR raw materials comprises mannitol, sucrose, chloride salt, bovine serum albumin, dNTPs, polyoxyethylene lauryl ether, HEPES, DNA polymerase, reverse transcriptase, RNase inhibitor, and water[[;]]
Claim 20. (Currently Amended) The system according to claim 11, wherein the diluent comprises polyol, chloride salt, Tris-HCl, surfactant, and water
REASONS FOR ALLOWANCE
The following is an examiner’s statement of reasons for allowance: the closest prior art to the instant application is United States Patent Application Publication US 2003/0162304 to Dority et al. (herein Dority) (X Reference on European Search Report) as cited on the 11/29/22 IDS and Chinese Publication CN109661273A to Briones et al. (herein Briones) (see machine translation provided).
Dority discloses a PCR reaction system and method for performing a PCR reaction, wherein the PCR reaction system comprises a sample containing unit 460 having a sample provided therein, the sample containing unit comprising a first liquid outlet/inlet; a diluent containing unit 470 having a diluent provided therein, the diluent containing unit 470 comprising a diluent outlet; a reagent chamber 478 comprising PCR raw materials; a PCR reaction unit 418 comprising a PCR reaction solution outlet and a sample mixture inlet; and a piston unit 416 comprising an injection chamber 450 and a piston 454, the injection chamber comprising a second liquid outlet/inlet, wherein the second liquid outlet/inlet is connected to the first liquid outlet/inlet through a first pipeline (440, 430, 438), the second liquid outlet/inlet is also connected to the diluent outlet through the first pipeline, the second liquid outlet/inlet is connected to the sample mixture inlet through a third pipeline (484, 486), and the PCR reaction solution outlet is also connected to the reagent chamber outlet through the first pipeline, wherein fluid passes from the diluent containing unit 470 through the diluent outlet, the first pipeline, and the second liquid outlet/inlet into the injection chamber, back through the second liquid outlet/inlet and first chamber into the reagent chamber 478, and through the sample mixture inlet into the third pipeline connected to the PCR reaction solution outlet, the method comprising: (i) subjecting the piston to a first movement processing, to allow a fluid sample from the sample containing unit 460 to enter the injection chamber 450; subjecting the piston to a second movement processing, to allow the fluid sample from the injection chamber 450 to enter the diluent containing unit 470 and a first mixing processing wherein the sample and lysing fluid moves into the injection chamber 450 for mixing; subjecting the piston to a third movement processing, to allow the product of the first mixing processing to ender the injection chamber 450; subjecting the piston to a fourth movement processing, to allow the product of the first mixing processing to enter the reagent chamber 478; subjecting the piston to a fifth movement processing wherein said product is subjected to a third mixing processing by toggling the mixture between the injection chamber 450 and the reagent chamber 478; subjecting the piston to a sixth movement processing wherein said mixture is transferred to the PCR reaction unit 418 for nucleic acid ampflication and/or detection in a thermal reaction chamber (see [0097-0104]; Figs. 25-26).
Briones discloses a PCR reaction system and method for performing a PCR reaction comprising a sample containing unit 1200, a diluent containing unit 1260, a pyrolysis module 1300/4300 comprising a reagent for a lysis solution in the form of a lyophilized powder; a PCR reaction unit 1900 comprising the reverse transcriptase in the form of a lyophilized powder for mixing with the product of a second mixing process from the pyrolysis module; a piston unit 1400 for controlling flow of fluid through the device and a ampflication module configured to perform a thermal cycling operation (see Fig. 10; [0127-0174]).
Neither Dority nor Briones, alone or in combination, teaches nor fairly suggests “a sample containing unit having a pyrolysis freeze-dried powder… the second liquid outlet/inlet is connected to the diluent outlet through a second pipeline, … the PCR reaction solution outlet is connected to the diluent through a fourth pipeline” as recited in instant independent claims 1 and 11 or  “ … subject the part of the diluent entering the injection chamber, the pyrolysis freeze-dried powder, and the sample to a first mixing processing, … wherein the first mixing processing is performed in the sample containing unit … subjecting a product of the first mixing processing to a pyrolysis processing, wherein the pyrolysis processing is performed in the sample containing unit; …subject the product of the pyrolysis processing entering the injection chamber and the remaining part of the diluent to a second mixing processing, wherein the second mixing processing is performed in the diluent containing unit” as recited in instant independent claim 1. In other words, the cited prior art fails to disclose the recited configuration and thus all the method steps of the claimed invention. Dority discloses a piston unit that can be rotated to connect to various units of the PCR reaction system through a single pipeline and therefore there would be no reason to modify the device of Dority to comprise the multiple connections of the claimed invention. Nor is there a teaching or suggestion in either prior art for the mixing, pyrolysis, etc. to occur in the sample containing unit followed by another mixing step in a diluent containing unit.
Any comments considered necessary by applicant must be submitted no later than the payment of the issue fee and, to avoid processing delays, should preferably accompany the issue fee.  Such submissions should be clearly labeled “Comments on Statement of Reasons for Allowance.”
Conclusion
